 NBA Roundup: Doncic fuels furious rally, Wemby falters in rough night

 A home loss for Victor Wembanyama, but an unbelievable comeback for Luka Doncic and Quentin Grimes
 By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net 
 Slovenia’s Luka Doncic paved the way for the Los Angeles Lakers in a 118–114 overtime victory versus the Charlotte Hornets at crypto.com Arena on Tuesday. With Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler sidelined, the six-time All-Star tallied 36 points, seven assists, six rebounds, one block, and one steal over 42 minutes to lock up a ninth straight win in the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season. Quentin Grimes set a new career high with 47 points on 10-of-14 three-point shooting, and drilled a buzzer-beating triple via a Doncic assist to force overtime, determined to complete a rally from an earlier 18-point deficit, with Georgian reserve Sandro Mamukelashvili chipping in three points. On the wrong side, French starter Moussa Diabate finished with five points and 16 rebounds, while German Christian Anderson Jr. had five points and French Tidjane Salaun went scoreless off the bench.
 Over in Texas, the Detroit Pistons ended the San Antonio Spurs ’ 12-game run by taking control after halftime for a 105–93 triumph at Frost Bank Center. French center Victor Wembanyama put up 25 points, 18 boards, four assists, one block, and one steal in 33 minutes. He created shots throughout the night, yet the Spurs struggled to contain their opponents in the paint.
 Late injuries soured the night further. With 53.6 seconds on the clock, Dylan Harper hit a wet spot on the floor and slipped into an awkward split. He grabbed at his groin and needed help getting to the locker room. Wemby also gave fans a brief scare, walking carefully to the sideline while holding his right leg.
 “It’s a terrible feeling, terrible sight. I know as much as you guys, so I hope he’s fine,” mentioned the 22-year-old big regarding 20-year-old Harper during his postgame press conference. “I’ll check on him today. But, yeah, I just hate this. I don’t know how else I can say this.” Head coach Mitch Johnson explained the medical staff lacked an official diagnosis.
 “I think it’s more on us,” Wembanyama previously recapped the team effort opposite the Pistons . “We didn’t do the right things. I think we should have been smarter.” 
 Knicks rally past Raptors, Rajakovic again
 At Scotiabank Arena, the defending champion New York Knicks climbed out of an early 13-point hole to beat the Toronto Raptors 111–102. The comeback mirrored Sunday’s overtime win and gave them a 15th straight victory over their Atlantic Division neighbor. Jalen Brunson dropped 31 points, and British starter OG Anunoby supplied 16. French teammates Pacome Dadiet and Mohamed Diawara stayed on the bench. Austrian big Jakob Poeltl managed three points for Toronto.
 Meanwhile, cameras caught Serbian play-caller Darko Rajakovic imitating Brunson for exaggerating contact during the match. Afterward, the 47-year-old addressed his roster’s late-game execution. “We’re learning what it means to win in a fourth quarter, and that fourth-quarter basketball is different,” he told reporters. “In the sense of referees, the whistle is going to tighten up. It’s going to be different. By that time, you’ve got to already know what the criteria in the game is. I think the fourth quarter comes down to simple execution, and it can be a little bit of luck.” 
 In Minneapolis, the Minnesota Timberwolves edged the Portland Trail Blazers 106–105 at Target Center. The visitors played without Israeli starter Deni Avdija, who sat out with left foot soreness, and let a late cushion slip away. LaMelo Ball picked off an inbound pass to set up Jaden McDaniels’ go-ahead layup with three seconds left, and Trey Lyles rejected Damian Lillard’s buzzer-beating attempt. The starting center of the Wolves , Rudy Gobert ran into foul trouble and failed to score, though French reserve Joan Beringer grabbed 13 rebounds alongside three points. Belgian Toumani Camara and French Sidy Cissoko recorded ten and six points as starters for Micah Nori.
 Out west at Intuit Dome, the Utah Jazz routed the Los Angeles Clippers 132–107 to snap a 12-game losing streak, with Brice Sensabaugh reaching 40 points and Ukrainian reserve Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk at eight. For the hosts, Italian Nick Martinelli and Spanish Baba Miller did not play until late in the fourth quarter, with the latter putting up a triple in garbage time.
